messages:
Ana Reyes: Heads-up — LumenDocs (onboarding, high QPS) flagged by alerts: 2x token cost yesterday and 95th pct tail latency spiking to ~850ms on requests >1024 tokens. I'm drafting a proactive performance plan.
Samir Patel: +1. Do we have traffic shape? repeated prefixes or many short requests?
Ana Reyes: Majority are long docs with repeated legal headers — so good candidate for prefix/KV caching. Also lots of similar system prompts across flows.
Devon Kim: Seeing the traces now — lots of small peaks from concurrent workers causing KV cache churn. We can stabilize with routing + cache retention tweaks.
Marta Lopez: Renewal is ~6w out — this is a good window to proactively reduce cost and show ops maturity. Can we scope a minimal change to lower unit cost before the renewal check-in?
Samir Patel: Proposed minimal plan: 1) enable prefix KV caching for their routes; 2) swap to a q4_0 quantized build of their current LlamaX model for inference-heavy endpoints; 3) add a fallback routing policy that sends non-critical bulk requests to a cheaper llama-lite model during spikes. Expected: ~30–40% cost drop, 20–45% tail latency reduction.
Kai Zhang: I can own the canary. Suggest canary rollout: 5% traffic to q4_0 variant for 24h, observe P50/P95/P99 + error rate.
Ana Reyes: Need a short customer note + enablement session to explain tradeoffs (slightly different tokenization/edge cases with q4) and ask for acceptance. Marta, can you schedule?
Marta Lopez: Booked tentative enablement for Tue 11am PT, I'll confirm.
Devon Kim: Ops checklist: increase KV cache TTL to 30s for the route, set batching window to 8ms, enable continuous batching. Also watch for increased decode time on a few long sequences with quantized kernels.
Samir Patel: Config snippet for routing/canary (for infra team):
```
routingPolicy:
  prefer_low_cost: false
  fallbacks:
    - model: llamaX-q4_0
      weight: 0.05
    - model: llama-lite-v1
      weight: 0.10
canary:
  target_pct: 5
  duration: 24h
cache:
  prefix_kv_ttl: 30s
  mode: prefer_kv
```
Kai Zhang: I'll create the canary job and add smoke tests (generate 10 long-doc prompts, check token/semantic diffs).
Ana Reyes: Customer note draft (short): "We found opportunities to reduce latency/cost by enabling prefix caching and running a small canary with a quantized model. We'll run a 5% canary for 24h and share results; no production rollback planned unless regressions show >2% semantic divergence." Thoughts?
Samir Patel: Fine. Also add a line: "expect minor tokenization delta on edge cases; we'll capture a testset and eval for semantic parity"
Devon Kim: Add dashboards: perf.redwood.com/team/lumendocs (I'll post a link when ready) — will include P50/P95/P99, cost per 1k tokens, and semantic-regression gating metric.
optimus-bot: [alert] LumenDocs onboarding: high-cost anomaly detected (24h). Incident ID: #LUM-2026-11-07-02
Marta Lopez: I'll handle scheduling + customer-facing slide deck (1 pager). Ana, can you collect the top 10 failing prompts we should include?
Ana Reyes: On it — will upload by EOD.
Kai Zhang: Timeline: canary infra + smoke tests today, canary tomorrow morning, results by EOD tomorrow.
Samir Patel: If canary looks good, recommend rolling to 50% over next 48h with monitoring and automated rollback on semantic diff >2% or error spike.
Ana Reyes: Thanks team — this is our play to de-risk renewal and surface measurable wins. I'll send the customer note after Marta confirms the meeting. :thumbsup:
